text:
sara: Heads-up — we saw a sequence of spot evictions in us-west this morning, ~20% of the cheaper pools. Several heavy models fell back to on-demand and p99 latency jumped. Anyone else seeing this?

jon: saw it in the autoscaler logs — eviction burst at 09:12->09:34. Warm nodes didn't spin up fast enough; warm-pool size is tuned for steady churn not spikes.

pei: rough numbers? did the router trigger variant fallback or cross-region fanout?

jon: routing fell through to on-demand for a few tenants, and to quantized variants for others. No cross-region fanout because threshold didn't hit.

amir: sounds like we need a more granular priority ladder per customer tier. Premium should get: dedicated -> warm pool -> local quantized variant -> cross-region warm. Standard: mixed spot -> local quantized variant -> cross-region preemptible.

olga: cross-region adds tail latency + cache cold starts. We should avoid it for short-lived evictions (<120s). Maybe only for sustained (>2m) or premium traffic.

pei: agreed. proposal: implement a dual-window policy: short-window soft spill (in-region, spill to busy nodes + KV warm reuse), long-window hard failover (cross-region warm or on-demand fallthrough). Also annotate responses with a "degraded" flag so clients know when quality changed.

jon: sketch of routing policy (for discussion):

```yaml
routing_policy:
  tiers:
    premium: [dedicated, warm_pool, quantized_variant, cross_region_warm]
    standard: [mixed_spot, quantized_variant, cross_region_preemptible]
  eviction_thresholds:
    short_window_s: 120
    long_window_s: 120
    eviction_rate_short: 0.08  # per-pool rate to trigger soft spill
    eviction_rate_long: 0.12   # sustained -> hard failover
  degrade_on_eviction: true
  client_signal: degraded=true
```

amir: we also need model-variant compatibility rules. can't degrade to quantized variant unless tokenizer + output post-process match. Add a verification step during model onboarding that writes a "fallback profile" with validated acceptance thresholds.

sara: +1. Also want cost guardrails: prefer warm_pool over cross-region because egress + cross-zone costs spike. Add cost weight to routing decisions, e.g. prefer cheaper option if latency penalty < 50ms.

olga: ops concern: warm pools need a warm cache priming job after a cross-region failover. We should pre-warm key KV prefixes for premium tenants when we decide to failover.

jon: canary plan: implement new routing in two phases — 1) internal canary for infra team traffic, 2) 10% premium traffic, evaluate for 48h. Metrics: eviction rate, p50/p95/p99, unit cost per token, and fraction of responses flagged degraded.

pei: small implementation note — router should expose an API to set per-tenant fallbackBudget and maxCrossRegionFallbacksPerHour so sales can configure SLAs.

infra-bot: deployment-note: rolling canary windows must not exceed 30m per step; use feature-flag "tiered-fanout-v2".

amir: client behavior: add explicit header so SDKs surface degraded state and optionally request automatic retry to fallback endpoint. We'll add to the SDK changelog.

sara: action items: jon => implement router changes + canary (48h), pei => add fallback-profile validation to model onboarding, amir => SDK degraded signal + docs, olga => design warm-pool prewarm job.

jon: I'll post a PR with routing config + test harness by EOD.

pei: i'll draft onboarding checks and a small test dataset for variant acceptance.

olga: I'll sketch prewarm lambda and cost estimate.

sara: thanks all. If we hit another eviction spike before canary is live, @oncall please escalate and temporarily raise warm_pool min-size for critical tenants. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: incident-log: evictions_us-west_1963456789 recorded -> notifications sent to #oncall.

jon: noted, tracking in the ticket: INFRA-7843.

sara: closing thread for now, will reopen if anything changes.
